newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway says no target level for crown vs mark.
newsitem.headline: Norway says no target level for crown vs mark.

text.p: A spokeswoman for the Norwegian Finance Ministry denied on Monday rumors that Finance Minister Jens Stoltenberg had targeted a level for the crown of between 4.10 and 4.30 against the mark.

The spokeswoman was reacting to reports from some news agencies that Stoltenberg, attending a meeting of Nordic and Baltic finance ministers in the west coast city of Bergen, had said that the central bank should bring the mark/crown back to a "stable" 4.10 to 4.30 range.
The crown sank heavily in afternoon trade hitting a low at 4.0785 against the mark. At 15.38 GMT it recovered slightly to 4.0675.
Anne-Sissel Skaanvik, spokeswoman in the Norwegian Finance Ministry, told Reuters in Bergen the minister did not say anything new and specified no figures.
Norway previously has said that the crown should in due time return to its previous strength before a strong appreciation in the petrocurrency in the second half of 1996.
Stoltenberg has never said what level that should be.
Norwegian policy is for the central bank, Norges Bank, to use monetary means to maintain a stable currency.
